Android does not show this request any more, because you refused the permission before. You can still turn it on from the app settings screen.
Microphone access for voice typing

WM Keyboard records audio only after you press the microphone button, and only while you speak. The recording goes to the speech recognition service that your Android settings select. That service turns the recording into text. On most phones that service is Google\'s, and Google can process the audio on its servers. An offline model keeps the audio on your device. The keyboard does not store the audio. Only the speech recognition service receives it. Voice typing is optional. Everything else on the keyboard works without it.
Camera access for the camera tool

WM Keyboard opens the camera only while the camera tool is on screen. You can take a photo and put it into the app that you type in. The keyboard writes the photo to its own private storage. The keyboard gives the photo to that app when you insert it. The keyboard uploads no photo, and sends no photo to the developer. The tool is optional.
Calendar access for the calendar tool

WM Keyboard reads your events. The calendar tool lists them, and you can insert one as text. The keyboard reads your calendar only while that tool is open. The keyboard never writes to your calendar. Your events stay on your device. The tool is optional.
Contacts access for name suggestions

WM Keyboard reads the names in your contacts. The names then complete as you type, and autocorrect does not change them. The keyboard keeps the names in memory while it runs, and writes them to no file. The names never leave your device. The setting is optional. It stays off until you turn it on.
Contacts access for email suggestions

WM Keyboard reads the email addresses in your contacts. When you type the start of an address, the keyboard offers the full address. The keyboard keeps the addresses in memory while it runs, and writes them to no file. The addresses never leave your device. The setting is optional. It stays off until you turn it on.
Photo access for screenshots in the clipboard

WM Keyboard watches for new screenshots and puts them in the clipboard. You can insert one without leaving the app you are in. Android has no permission for screenshots alone, so it gives access to all of your photos. The keyboard looks only at new screenshots. The images stay on your device. The keyboard inserts an image only when you press it. The setting is optional. It stays off until you turn it on.
Storage access to save to your gallery

On Android 9 and older, the keyboard needs storage permission to save an image to your gallery. The old Android permission also covers reading your storage. The keyboard writes only the image that you ask it to save. The keyboard reads nothing and uploads nothing. Newer Android versions do not need this permission.
Notification access for media controls

Android gives the play, pause and skip controls only to apps with notification access. The media tool needs that access. For this tool the keyboard\'s notification listener reads no notification, no title, no sender and no content. It exists only so that Android lets the tool see the current media session. The same access also powers the optional one-time code chip in Typing settings. Only while that is turned on does the listener read notification text, on your device, to find a verification code. The keyboard stores nothing, and nothing leaves your device. The system screen you are about to open describes the full access that this permission can give. This app uses it for these two features and nothing else. Both are optional.
Notification access for one-time codes

When a verification code arrives in a notification, the keyboard can offer it as a chip above the keys, one tap from typed. To see the code arrive, the keyboard needs notification access. While the feature is on, the keyboard reads the text of incoming notifications on your device to find a code. The code is kept only in memory, only for a few minutes, and is never sent anywhere. The same access also powers the optional media tool, which reads no notification content. The system screen you are about to open describes the full access that this permission can give. This app uses it for these two features and nothing else. Turn the feature off and the keyboard stops reading notifications at once.
Usage access for clipboard source apps

With usage access, the keyboard records which app was in front when you copied something. It shows that app when you press and hold the clip. The keyboard reads the front app only at the moment of a copy. It does not read your history or your time in an app. The keyboard keeps the answer with the clip, on your device only. Nothing about your app usage leaves your device. The setting is optional. It stays off until you turn it on.
Permission to install updates

To install a new version, Android must let this app install apps. The app uses that permission for one thing: a new version of itself that you downloaded from the project releases page and pressed Install on. Before it asks, the app compares the file against the checksum in the release and against the key this install is signed with. Android shows its own confirmation for the first update. The app never installs another app, and it never installs anything you did not press Install on.
Display over other apps, for the keyboard button

With this permission the keyboard can draw one small round button over other apps while the keyboard is closed. Tap the button and the keyboard opens, even on a screen with no text field, so you can send keys and shortcuts to that app. The button is the only thing the keyboard draws with this permission. It cannot see or read what is on screen, and it collects no data. Android\'s settings screen describes everything this permission allows. The keyboard uses it for this button and nothing else. The button is optional and stays off until you turn it on.
Accessibility service for keyboard gestures

This service keeps the keyboard gestures available while a screen reader runs. The gestures are the spacebar cursor slide, the backspace word swipe, glide typing and handwriting. Only an accessibility service can arrange this. The service subscribes to no accessibility events. It cannot read window content. It marks nothing but the keyboard\'s own key grid. It collects no data. Android\'s accessibility screen warns about the full power of this category. This service declares none of that power.
